name: Roskilde University
about: Roskilde University was set up in 1972 to experiment with how knowledge is taught, and it still works differently from every other Danish university. You do not apply to a named subject. You apply to one of three broad international bachelor programmes, spend the whole first year in an interdisciplinary basic studies section, and only then choose the two bachelor subjects you will study for the remaining two years. Roughly half of all study time is group project work on real problems rather than lectures and exams, and the campus at Trekroner, 30 minutes by train from Copenhagen, has about 7,900 students.
ibNotes: RUC lists the International Baccalaureate among the international qualifications that satisfy its general admission requirement, but its English pages do not publish a minimum IB point score or a subject-by-subject IB-to-Danish conversion table.
RUC does not publish an IB results-service (IBIS) institution code on its English admission pages.
If your qualification is not on RUC's list, you can ask RUC for a pre-assessment or have it assessed by the Danish Agency for Higher Education and Science.
quotaNotes: RUC runs a guaranteed-admission scheme rather than relying only on a published cut-off: "if you meet all admission requirements and you have the equivalent of the required Danish GPA, you are guaranteed admission." For the 2026 intake the guaranteed-admission GPAs were 2.0 for International Bachelor in Natural Sciences, 8.5 for Global Humanities and 9.0 for International Bachelor in Social Sciences. Guaranteed admission is not available to applicants holding qualifications from outside the EU/EEA, because "your grades cannot be converted directly to the Danish grading scale"; those applicants are assessed in quota 2.

deadlines.label: Application (IB and all international qualifications)
deadlines.notes: optagelse.dk is open from 1 February to 15 March, 12 noon CET. This deadline covers IB, European Baccalaureate, Danish/French Baccalaureate and exemption-based applications.

deadlines.label: Application fee payment (non-EU/EEA)
deadlines.notes: EUR 200 (DKK 1,490). Refunded only if you are admitted and registered as an active student on 1 September of the year of admission.

deadlines.label: Vacant study places open
deadlines.notes: Non-EU/EEA citizens who need a study residence permit cannot apply for vacant places.

tuitionNonEu: Entry September 2026: Global Humanities and Social Sciences EUR 10,000 per year (EUR 5,000 per semester, EUR 30,000 for the full degree); Natural Sciences EUR 16,000 per year (EUR 8,000 per semester, EUR 48,000 for the full degree). Application fee EUR 200. EU/EEA and Swiss citizens pay nothing.

notes: RUC's structure is the thing to understand before applying. You apply to a broad programme, not to a named subject. Year one is a shared interdisciplinary basic studies section; years two and three are spent on two bachelor subjects you choose at the end of year one. Your degree title is the combination.

Because the subject choice happens after you arrive, the entry requirements listed here are for the programme as a whole. Individual bachelor subjects can carry additional requirements — RUC publishes these separately under 'Additional specific admission requirements for bachelor's subjects' (https://ruc.dk/en/additional-specific-admission-requirements-bachelors-subjects). Check the subject you have in mind before you assume you qualify.
About half of all study time at RUC is group project work rather than taught classes and written exams.

RUC states hour minimums as well as levels for each required subject, for example English 210 hours, Mathematics A 375 hours, Chemistry 190 hours, Biotechnology A 400 hours, Geoscience A 400 hours. If your IB subject hours fall short you may be asked to supplement.
The guaranteed-admission GPAs quoted here are 2026 figures and are not the same thing as a quota 1 cut-off; RUC does not publish quota 1 cut-offs for these programmes on its English pages.

programmes.name: International Bachelor in Natural Sciences
programmes.summary: You spend the first year on a shared science foundation — maths, experimental work and project work across disciplines — and only then pick the two subjects you will graduate in, from Bioprocess Science, Chemistry, Computer Science, Environmental Biology, Mathematics, Molecular Biology and Physics. Choose this if you are strong at science but not yet sure whether you want to be a chemist, a programmer or a biologist.
programmes.requirementsText: English at Danish B-level. Mathematics at Danish A-level. One of the following combinations: Physics B and Chemistry B; Physics B and Biotechnology A; Chemistry B and Geoscience A; or Chemistry B and Biology A and Physics C.
extraRequirements: Guaranteed admission in 2026 for applicants who met all requirements and had a Danish-converted GPA of at least 2.0.
Guaranteed admission is not open to applicants with non-EU/EEA qualifications.

programmes.name: International Bachelor in Social Sciences
programmes.summary: A first year of interdisciplinary social science — economics, politics, organisations and methods — followed by two years in two chosen subjects from Business Administration, Business Studies, International Studies, Communication Studies, Cultural Encounters and Social Psychology of Everyday Life. It is the RUC route for students who want business or politics but want to keep two options open rather than commit to one now.
programmes.requirementsText: English at Danish B-level. Mathematics at Danish B-level. History or Social Science or Contemporary History or History of Ideas at Danish B-level. You must also meet one of the following minimum grade requirements: a grade point average of at least 6.0 on the Danish 7-point grading scale from your entry qualification, or an average of at least 4.0 on the Danish 7-point grading scale in English and Mathematics combined.
extraRequirements: A minimum grade requirement applies: either an overall GPA of 6.0 on the Danish 7-point scale, or an average of 4.0 across English and Mathematics.
Guaranteed admission in 2026 for applicants who met all requirements and had a Danish-converted GPA of at least 9.0.
Guaranteed admission is not open to applicants with non-EU/EEA qualifications.

programmes.name: Bachelor in Global Humanities
programmes.summary: The first year covers the humanities in four broad dimensions — culture, text, history and subjectivity — before you choose two bachelor subjects from Communication Studies, Cultural Encounters, Social Psychology of Everyday Life, Business Studies and International Studies. It suits students interested in culture, media and how people make sense of the world, and who want to combine that with something applied.
programmes.requirementsText: English at Danish B-level. History or History of Ideas or Contemporary History at Danish B-level. One additional language — either a beginner's language at Danish A-level or an advanced language at Danish B-level. The additional language cannot be English or the language of instruction of your upper secondary education.
extraRequirements: The second foreign language must be at Danish B level if it is a continued language, or Danish A level if you began it from scratch; it cannot be English or your school's language of instruction.
Guaranteed admission in 2026 for applicants who met all requirements and had a Danish-converted GPA of at least 8.5.
Guaranteed admission is not open to applicants with non-EU/EEA qualifications.
